problem: The level-4 box is labelled '2 rows' but its note says 'final adder'. The step from 3 rows to 2 rows is itself one carry save adder (3:2 counter). The final carry propagate adder comes after those 2 rows, so the figure contradicts the text ('four reduction levels', CPA is not a reduction level). The caption adds to the confusion by saying 'The last box is the final carry propagate adder' when the last box is labelled '2 rows'.
fix: Change the level-4 note to '1 CSA' and draw the final carry propagate adder as a separate box after the '2 rows' box, labelled 'final CPA (not a reduction level)'.

problem: 'A carry save adder (CSA) takes three bits of the same weight' describes a full adder, not a CSA. A CSA takes three N-bit operands and produces a sum word and a carry word; one full adder handles one bit column. The next sentence ('A full adder is one column of a CSA') corrects this, but the opening definition is loose and a student may quote the wrong version in the exam.
fix: Write: 'A CSA takes three N-bit numbers and produces two N-bit numbers, a sum word and a carry word. In each bit column one full adder adds three bits of the same weight and gives a sum bit of that weight and a carry bit of twice that weight. That column is a 3:2 counter.'
